- Model consistently underestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after recent spikes.
- Overestimates in the middle of the forecast horizon, particularly after sharp upward moves.
- Tends to lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days, especially in downward trends.
- Shows strong mean reversion bias — forecasts often overshoot peaks and fail to capture sustained trends.
- Underestimates volatility in low-price regimes; fails to anticipate sharp drops or rebounds.
- Overconfident in short-term forecasts; fails to adjust for seasonal or policy-driven price shifts.
- In high-price regimes, model tends to overpredict decline, underpredict rebound.
- Forecasts are more accurate when prices are stable or trending slowly; poor performance during rapid volatility.
